title: Key Account Signal Admittance Protocol (Mercury)
creator: Diego Morales
description: Introduce a deterministic, auditable protocol (codename: Mercury) to admit, score, route, and commit to roadmap items originating from high-value/key accounts and escalations. Mercury defines signal inputs, admission thresholds, SLAs for triage, stakeholder handoffs, and a small-commit playbook to reduce impulse commits while ensuring predictable treatment for strategic customers.
problem_statement: Enterprise customers and strategic partners escalate feature asks through multiple channels (CS, Sales, Support, Success), creating inconsistent intake, overpromising, and unclear runway for PM/Eng. Current ad-hoc escalations cause churn in sprint commitments and opaque prioritization for engineering and executives.
goals: Formalize a single admission gate for key-account feature escalations
Provide transparent scoring and routing to roadmap lanes (Fastpass / Advocacy / Standard)
Ensure SLAs for initial triage and follow-up communications (48h triage target)
Reduce in-cycle scope churn from escalations by 60% within two cycles
Tie admitted items to measurable signals (revenue at risk, renewal timing, strategic partnership) for reporting and OKR rollups
success_metrics: Time to first triage response (target <= 48 hours)
Percentage reduction in mid-cycle scope adds attributed to escalations (target -60%)
Share of admitted signals with committable scope and clear acceptance criteria (target >= 80%)
Executive satisfaction score for escalation handling (surveyed net promoter >= 7)
Correlation: admitted items -> roadmap commit or scheduled investigation within 3 cycles (target >= 70%)
acceptance_criteria: Mercury scoring algorithm defined and documented (signal weights and thresholds)
Triage playbook with owners and communication templates produced
Console intake form and CS/Sales intake flow wireframes approved
Alerting/telemetry for key-account escalations integrated into ops dashboard
Pilot with 3 strategic accounts and CS team executed, with post-pilot retrospective
proposed_scoring_factors: Revenue or ARR impact (renewal timing multiplier)
Product fit delta (how much product change is required)
Customer strategic value (partner, reference, co-sell potential)
Risk of churn or contract downgrade (probability-weighted)
routing_lanes: Immediate Commitment (can be slotted into next release with a negotiated scope)
Advocacy Roadmap (queued for prioritization with explicit tradeoffs)
No-Admit / Product Mismatch (documented disposition + CS playbook)
Escalation to Execs (only when score > executive threshold and org impact)
tasks: Draft Mercury PRD and scoring rubric — owner: Asha Patel
Design intake form and email templates — owner: Minh Tran (Design)
Implement intake webhook and logging in Console — owner: Suresh Iyer (Eng)
Add Mercury signals to roadmap dashboard and report — owner: Priya Shah (Analytics)
Run 3-account pilot and collect feedback — owner: Diego Morales (PM)
Create training session and one-pager for CS, Sales, Success — owner: Hannah Lee (RevOps)
Define SLA enforcement and escalation workflow in Policy docs — owner: Legal & Compliance review
timeline: Phase 1 (2 weeks): PRD + scoring rubric. Phase 2 (4 weeks): wireframes + engineering stub + telemetry. Phase 3 (6 weeks): pilot with 3 accounts and retro. Finalize rollout in cycle 2026-W18.
rollout_plan: Internal alpha with CS and one pilot CSM
Closed beta with 3 strategic customers (use cases across retention, regulatory, partnership)
Refinement based on pilot metrics and feedback
Quarterly review and score recalibration tied to OKR outcomes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-indexing revenue signals leads to neglect of platform improvements — Mitigation: quota reserved for non-revenue SLO items
Risk: Engineering workload spikes from commitments — Mitigation: timeboxed commitment windows and bounded-scope CLAs
Risk: Perceived favoritism by customers — Mitigation: published admission rubric and standardized communication templates
Risk: Misuse of Exec escalation — Mitigation: Exec gate requires documented score + VP sponsor approval
dependencies: Legal-575 (contract amendment template for committed scope)

notes: Mercury is intentionally conservative: admission != commitment. Admission should guarantee transparent follow-up and a bounded decision window rather than immediate inclusion in a sprint unless pre-negotiated.
outcome_expectation: If successful, Mercury will reduce ad-hoc engineering churn, increase predictability for strategic customers, and provide a feed of customer-priority items into OKR cadence with measurable ROI evidence.
